title: Put a cup on a tray
instruction: Put the cup on the tray.
context: Placing a cup upright and fully on a tray is the first step of serving or clearing a table in a restaurant, hospital or care home.
setup: Two YAM arms at a table (top 74.75 cm above the floor), bases at y = +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. A dark paper takeaway coffee cup with a printed logo and a fitted lid, 8 cm across at its widest and 12.6 cm tall with the lid on (50 g), stands upright 17 cm in front of the arm bases and 12 cm left of centre. A grey wooden tray, modeled as a flat board 20 cm deep, 16 cm wide and 2 cm thick (300 g), lies flat 25 cm in front of the arm bases and 5 cm right of centre, its edges parallel to the table's. Both are loose. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: 1.0 if, at the end, the cup's centre is at least 4 cm (half the cup's width) inside every edge of the tray, its bottom is within 1 cm of the tray's top surface, its axis is within 10 degrees of upright, and the cup and tray are both still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 second. 0.5 if the cup's centre is over the tray and its bottom is within 1 cm of the tray's top surface, but it fails the 4 cm or 10-degree conditions. 0.0 otherwise.
fidelity: Approximate: the cup is a rigid, lidded paper-cup model with nothing inside it, colliding as a single convex shape, and the tray is a flat rigid board with no rim. Friction and mass are nominal values. The scorer cannot see the grippers, so a cup still held motionless on the tray is not distinguished; on a real table, open the grippers before scoring.
